transcript: Teachers can get free packages of printable logic puzzles, made for their class. This short video shows every step, from the request form to the PDFs in your inbox. On thelogicgrid.com, choose For educators, at the top of the game page. The Educators page explains the four steps. Fill in the form, confirm your school email, our team reviews your request, and your puzzles arrive by email. Start with your name, your school email address, your school and your role. Use your school address, not a personal one: we send a code there to confirm that you are an educator.

Choose your students' grade level. The page shows what suits that grade: the difficulty, the size of the grid, how much story to read, and whether to use large print. Then say how many different puzzles you need, up to thirty. Choose the difficulty: suited to the grade, building up from easier to harder, or one level for every puzzle. You can also choose the grid size, how many questions go under each puzzle, and even the kinds of clues. Pick any of our themes, with a topic for each, or tick none for a mix of them all. You can type your students' first names, too, and they become the characters in the stories.

Or choose Create my own theme. Start from an example, or write your own story, characters and up to four categories, each with its items. We build the grid, the clues and the answer key from it, and check that every puzzle has exactly one answer. Under Printing, choose the paper size, where the answer keys go, worked solutions, large print, and a title for your package. Tick the box to agree to use the puzzles with your own students, then press Send my request. The page now asks for a six-digit code. Check your school email.

The email has your code, and a button that confirms your address in one click. The code works for two days. If it does not arrive, look in your spam folder, or ask for a new code. Type the code and press Confirm. That's it. Your request is now with our team, and the page gives you a request number. A person on our team checks each request, usually within a day or two, and approves it. Once it is approved, your puzzles are made and emailed to you within minutes, as PDF files ready to print.

Each package starts with a cover page: how to use the puzzles, and a list of them all. Every puzzle has a brand new story, written at the right level for the grade, with the clues, a blank grid and the questions. The answer keys come in their own file, so you can keep them back, with a step by step solution if you asked for one. The email with your puzzles also has a private link to your own ideas, problems and feedback section. It starts with a two-minute survey about how our tools can help your class. Send us an idea, a problem or feedback any time, and see our answers right there.
Our team reads every note, answers in plain words, and emails you the answer. Fill in the form, confirm your email, and print. Happy puzzling!
